GoPro surges 22% and extends a 120% monthly run on its Starman Optical merger, while Coherent gains 6% anchored by real datacenter revenue.

SPY slides 0.4% and QQQ trades flat as GoPro prices in an unproven optical stub trading well above the deal's $1.14 cash value.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Optical-photonics stocks are running Friday morning, along with a stock that's commonly associated with cameras and accessories, even as broad benchmarks slip. Notably, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.33% to $770.59, and the NASDAQ 100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is essentially flat at $718.38.

janitors / Flickr

GoPro (NASDAQ:GPRO) stock is up 34% to $1.86, extending a rerating that began Monday on the company's Starman Optical merger news. Meanwhile, Coherent (NYSE:COHR) stock is up 7% to $282.45, giving the AI-connectivity theme a listed anchor with real datacenter revenue behind it. Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) stock is up 3% to $876.92, rounding out the incumbent optical set with a comparatively milder session gain.

The category itself is bid up today, and GoPro's move is continuation of a deal already in the tape. The transaction was disclosed earlier in the week, so today's flow is driven by positioning and enthusiasm around the pivot into optical, with no fresh operating disclosure attached.

Starman Merger Terms and a Markiplier Stake

GoPro agreed on Monday to merge with Starman Optical, a privately held U.S. maker of optical transceivers. Under the terms, GoPro shareholders receive an aggregate $285 million, or $1.14 per share in cash, and retain roughly 10% of the combined company's outstanding shares. GoPro said the transaction also extinguishes roughly $92 million of outstanding debt. The combined entity keeps its Nasdaq listing and is expected to close by year-end, subject to regulatory and stockholder approval.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Ad-tech is splitting into winners and stragglers at midday, it seems. The Trade Desk (NASDAQ:TTD) stock is slumping faster than the stock market overall as the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is only down 0.31% to $770.78. Meanwhile, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 0.15% to $718.76.

Programmatic peers Magnite (NASDAQ:MGNI) and AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP) form the natural comparison set for today's move. The Trade Desk announced plans to reduce its total workforce by 15% as part of an organizational realignment, redirecting resources toward higher-priority growth areas and operational effectiveness. The reduction is expected to be substantially completed during Q3 2026, and The Trade Desk expects to incur $39 million to $51 million in cash restructuring and related charges, primarily for employee severance and benefits.

SCHG's top three holdings are NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft, and together they control nearly a third of the fund, turning a "diversified" growth ETF into a concentrated three-stock bet.

SCHG trailed QQQ by 7 points year-to-date while its index capped Palantir at 1% weight despite the AI darling posting 93% revenue growth.

Investors wanting purer exposure to today's top performers should consider QQQ, while SCHG suits those comfortable with a mega-cap-tilted, factor-scored growth basket.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

The Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Growth ETF (NYSEARCA:SCHG) devotes 9.83% of the fund to Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), a position larger than its holdings in Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) at 3.91%, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) at 3.45%, and Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) at 1.25% combined.

24/7 Wall St.

SCHG holds nearly two hundred stocks, but that label understates what an investor actually owns.

The Apple weighting is only the start. NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) sits on top at 11.01%, Apple next at 9.83%, and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) at 7.17%. Three companies control close to a third of the portfolio. Anyone who bought SCHG for diversified exposure across a large growth basket got something narrower: a three-stock bet wearing broader packaging.

Gap Growth Investors Did Not Sign Up For

Through the September 3 close, SCHG returned 10.12% year-to-date on a price basis. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) returned 13.38%, and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) returned 16.83%. A fund built for growth trailed a broad-market benchmark by roughly 3 points and lost to the Nasdaq-100 by nearly 7 points. The concentration numbers only partly explain that gap.

That said, there's more to the underperformance.

Blaming Apple alone would be lazy analysis. Apple rose 21.06% year to date, aided by a $109.4 billion June quarter that CEO Tim Cook called "our strongest June quarter ever, with double-digit revenue growth across iPhone, Mac and Services". NVIDIA rose 22.64% after data center revenue grew 117% year over year. Those two positions helped SCHG.

QQQ
SPY
BITO
^GSPC

The broad market exchange-traded fund SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) was up 0.03%, and the actively traded Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) advanced 0.5% in Friday's premarket activity, as the August jobs report topped estimates.

US stock futures were mixed, with S&P 500 Index futures down 0.24%, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures slipping 0.34%, and Nasdaq futures gaining 0.5% before the start of regular trading.

Nonfarm payrolls jumped by 162,000, well above the 55,000 jobs increase expected in a survey compiled by Bloomberg as of 7:15 am ET.

The unemployment rate remained at 4.1%, as expected, while the labor force participation rate rose to 61.6% from 61.4% in July and the size of the labor force surged.

In premarket action, bitcoin was up by 1%. Among cryptocurrency ETFs, the cryptocurrency fund ProShares Bitcoin Strategy ETF (BITO) was 2.8% lower, Ether ETF (EETH) was down 2.91%, and Bitcoin & Ether Market Cap Weight ETF (BETH) was flat.

Power Play:

Consumer

The State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLP) was down 0.38, the Vanguard Consumer Staples Index Fund ETF Shares (VDC) was down 0.07, and the iShares US Consumer Staples ETF (IYK) was up 0.8%. The State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY) lost 0.64%. The VanEck Retail ETF (RTH) was inactive, while the State Street SPDR S&P Retail ETF (XRT) was inactive.

Tesla (TSLA) shares were down 3.2% pre-bell after Future Fund Managing Director Gary Black Gary Black on X called the Cybercab event "largely a bust" because of its limited deployment details and the lack of a livestream.

The autonomous cab service also came under investigation by the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration over the process used to claim compliance with federal vehicle safety standards.

Winners and Losers:

Technology

The State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) gained 0.7%, the iShares US Technology ETF (IYW) was roughly 0.5% higher, and the iShares Expanded Tech Sector ETF (IGM) was up 0.02%. Among semiconductor ETFs, the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) rose by more than 1.3%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) rose by 1.9%.

Nvidia (NVDA) shares were up almost 1% in premarket activity after the company said its RTX platform is gaining new tools to simplify local AI agent deployment and also increased its equity investments to $99 billion, CNBC reported Friday.

The company is also reportedly expected to invest billions of dollars in AI developer Thinking Machines Lab, The Information reported Thursday, citing the firm's existing investor, Andreessen Horowitz.

Health Care

The State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) dropped 0.2%, the Vanguard Health Care Index Fund (VHT) was down 1.2%, while the iShares US Healthcare ETF (IYH) slipped 0.2%. The iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB) gained 0.03%.

Novo Nordisk (NVO) stock was down 2.2% premarket after the company said its charitable foundation and its Quantum Foundry Copenhagen company are planning to set up a new 5,300-square-meter quantum chip production facility in Copenhagen.

Financial

The State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) was down 0.4%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X Shares (FAS) was up nearly 1%, while its counterpart, Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X Shares (FAZ), was over 1.1% higher.

Robinhood Markets (HOOD) shares traded down 3.7% in early-hours activity after AMC Entertainment (AMC) CEO Adam Aron criticized Robinhood Markets (HOOD) on the recently launched tokenized version of AMC shares, referring to the practice as "contemptible" and "outrageous".

Industrial

The State Street Industrial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLI) advanced almost 0.1%, while the Vanguard Industrials Index Fund (VIS) and the iShares US Industrials ETF (IYJ) were inactive.

GE Vernova (GEV) stock was up 0.6% before the opening bell after the company reported a deal with the Venezuelan government that is expected to help stabilize the country's power grid within a year by adding 1 gigawatt of new power, several media outlets reported Thursday, citing US Energy Secretary Chris Wright.

Energy

The iShares US Energy ETF (IYE) retreated by around 0.1%, while the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE) was down by 0.6%.

NextEra Energy (NEE) stock was down 0.4% before the market open after Dominion Energy (D) and NextEra said shareholders have given consent to proceed with a planned merger between the companies, according to regulatory filings Thursday.

Commodities

Front-month US West Texas Intermediate crude oil retreated by 0.7% to $90.93 per barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange. Natural gas was up 0.3% to $2.92 per 1 million British Thermal Units. The United States Oil Fund (USO) decreased by 1%, while the United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was 1.1% higher.

Gold futures for November retreated by 0.5% to $4,515.20 an ounce on the Comex. Silver futures lost 0.3% to $67.49 an ounce. SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) was down by almost 0.1%, and the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) dropped by 0.04%.

UiPath (NYSE:PATH) stock is sinking in Friday morning trading after fiscal second-quarter results delivered a headline beat but the forward guide implied a sharp deceleration. The reaction stands out on a session where large-cap tech is holding firm.

The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 0.5% to $721.08, keeping the NASDAQ 100 comfortably green. Meanwhile, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.1% to $772.31. UiPath stock is down 14% to $15.69, unwinding a chunk of the rally that had UiPath shares up 29% over the past month through Thursday's close.

Momentum had been squarely on UiPath's side heading into the release, which set an elevated bar for the guide. Cutting the growth rate nearly in half for the coming quarter after a headline beat is precisely the setup that produces a re-rating morning like this one.

Guidance Overshadows a Clean Beat

UiPath reported Q2 CY2026 revenue of $410.3 million against a $397.9 million consensus, up 13.4% year over year, with adjusted earnings of $0.15 per share in line with estimates. Adjusted operating income landed at $89.03 million against a $75.22 million consensus, a wide beat that showcases the margin discipline management has emphasized all year. The company also lifted its full-year revenue guidance to $1.79 billion at the midpoint from $1.78 billion.
